X-198 — a discrepancy is reviewed, never corrected: reconciliation_runs carries reviewed_at/reviewed_by_user_id, GatewayEngine::reviewDiscrepancy refuses a balanced run (NothingToReviewException) and is idempotent on a reviewed one, the numbers on the run are never written again; the screen lists discrepancy_logged runs only and the cross-account roll-up is a finished waiting state (OWNER ACTION 15, X-198 anchor). X-201 — a dispute is never submitted empty: DisputeDefenseEngine::submit refuses unless the bundle is compiled (DisputeNotCompiledException), the queue compiles the invoice line plus the tenant's note, the outcome is a closed set (won/lost) through DisputeOutcomeAction and a loss records the clawback; evidence from telephony and signature capture and the deadline from the gateway's webhook are finished waiting states (G1-08, X-201 anchor). X-120 — the vault's door takes the number, the expiry and the name and keeps none of them: CardPresentAction checks Luhn, the month, the expiry and the name, derives brand and last four, writes no row, dispatches no event and logs nothing, and answers waiting_on_tokenisation; the screen clears the number in a finally so it is never round-tripped, and the finished state is 'Waiting on Stripe tokenisation' until Stripe Elements or a tokenisation contract exists; the security code has no field of any name (N-046, N-047, N-120-01, P-196, ruling 20/21). X-173 — the conflicts list is where a person closes a sync conflict and the only place: AccountingSyncEngine::resolveConflict answers status refused for a blank or 'uncategorised' answer (posting to uncategorised is not a resolution) and for a resolved row (a resolution is not overwritten silently), status resolved otherwise — an array answer, not an exception, is the module's shape; the sync path never calls it, so a conflict row is never auto-closed (anchor, §141.5); no event — a person's decision is not an inference; sync.conflict (§141.5) is absent from the generated manifest, UNRESOLVED on Track 1's scaffold. the late-fee term is a ROW on ar_plan_terms — late_fee_percent and late_fee_cap_cents, nullable, beside the plan threshold; null means the agreement names no late fee and ArEngine::applyLateFee throws FeeWithoutTermException before any write (G1-71); the percent and the cap replace the engine's 10 % / $50 literal (P-193). Rejected: a per-invoice term column (the agreement is the tenant's terms; X-121's quote is Track 1's spine, ruling 8); keeping the literal (P-193); a caller-supplied hasTerm flag (ruling 15 — a refusal clause is not a refusal). Consequence: a tenant with no term written gets no late fee until the owner writes one. Test: X211Test::test_a_fee_with_no_matching_term_is_refused

the ageing screen is the fee door and the term door — the late-fee term is written on the page through ArSetLateFeeTermAction (ArEngine::setLateFeeTerm, updateOrCreate on the tenant's ar_plan_terms row, ArLateFeeTermSet emitted; percent 1–100 required, cap optional), and a fee is applied per overdue row through ArApplyLateFeeAction; FeeWithoutTermException is rendered as a finished attention state on the same page, never swallowed (G1-71, P-193). Rejected: the term on the paymentplan builder (that page is the schedule threshold, not the fee); a default term seeded on tenant provisioning (a tenant with no term written gets no fee — the R245 decision of 03:34); a fee button with no amount (the amount is the owner's, the cap is the row's). Consequence: the first fee a tenant applies is refused until the term is written on the same screen. Test: AgeingByReasonScreenTest::test_a_late_fee_is_refused_without_a_term_and_applied_inside_it

R245: an overflow is recorded charged only when the gateway issued a charge id - GatewayEngine::capture calls a processor only for a stripe connection and otherwise returns a payment awaiting_processor without throwing, so deriving charged from the absence of an exception told the owner the card on file had covered money that never moved.

a capture is announced only when the gateway issued a charge id — PaymentCaptured fires from GatewayEngine::capture() only on a non-null gateway_charge_id, because capture() makes no external call for a non-stripe connection and an event named for a capture that did not happen propagates to every future listener.

a partial payment records the money and nothing else - recordPayment derives the invoice status from paid_cents against total_cents instead of writing paid unconditionally, because every unpaid and overdue query filters on status before the paid_cents clause, so a partially paid invoice left the Unpaid screen, the ageing and the overdue chase while the customer still owed the balance.

a partial offline payment keeps the reason the invoice was being chased - logOfflinePayment writes the invoice's own status on the losing branch instead of the issued literal, because ReceivableState moves to current only on paid, so a part-paid overdue invoice read issued while the receivable still said the account was being chased

the paid-today tile names the invoice value it sums rather than cash received - the screen totals total_cents over invoices that became paid today, and no per-instalment receipt date is stored anywhere in this lane, so the label states what is computed and the screen names the missing dependency

the revenue-recovery row names the credit it sums rather than money recovered - the figure sums topup and grant ledger entries, the top-up button on the same row grants credit and takes no card, and LedgerGrantAction has no caller outside the tests, so nothing on this ladder is money that came back

the dunning ladder prints its service settings as a recorded intent rather than a state - phone_answering, ai_enabled and voicemail_only are written by advanceDunning and read by no code that switches a phone or an agent, so the row says what the ladder set and not what the account is doing

the storefront says stock comes off when the order is placed rather than when it is paid - checkoutCart decrements inventory_quantity in the same transaction that creates the order pending_payment, and ruling 45 leaves no path to paid, so the cart header and the checkout waiting state now say what the engine does and name cancel as the only way back

the cart line says the cart expires rather than that stock is reserved - addToCart never touches inventory_quantity and its sold-out guard counts only this cart, so two sessions can each hold the last unit, and the only thing expires_at governs is the cart row itself

the declines tile and empty state name the window they are showing - the startOfWeek and deferral filters are both inside the showAll branch, so a tile headed this week counted every decline ever the moment the owner pressed Show all
